r0-context.title: Load baseline context
r0-context.imperative: Read your inherited global doctrine (this skill's references/global-crew.md and references/global-everyone.md), then the project deltas if present: docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md, docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md, plus the handoff, the diff, and the relevant packet. Record pass when loaded.
r0-context.finding: Loaded global-crew.md + global-everyone.md (installed reviewer skill), docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md, the g1-review handoff, and the full working-tree diff of scripts/checklist_engine.py (+64/-1) and tests/test_checklist_engine.py (+154). CREW_CONTEXT deltas that bind this review: python-not-py; a check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from one that passed (so the RED must be reproduced by mutating the tree); assert against behaviour not text.

r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding: Every task-statement clause is satisfied and independently checked: populated directives reach the agent through current (reproduced live on the run's own spine.json and on the shipped COMMANDER_SPINE); the golden is over the ACTUAL shipped template, not a lookalike fixture, and I reproduced its RED; a dedicated formatter sits beside _render_anchor_lines rather than reusing it (decision:own-helper-not-anchors-helper honored); the first ACTIVE line is byte-identical corpus-wide; absent/empty stay silent, guard-proven; state() stays pure. The implementer also caught that the handoff's abbreviated example showed four contract fields where the shipped gate carries six, and wrote the golden over the real six -- I confirmed all six render.

r2-scope.title: Scope drift
r2-scope.imperative: Did the change stay inside allowed scope and respect specific exclusions? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r2-scope.finding: No scope drift and no excluded file touched. git status --porcelain shows exactly two tracked source files modified, scripts/checklist_engine.py and tests/test_checklist_engine.py; everything else is .agent-work engine state and crew artifacts, which the handoff explicitly rules out of scope. Each named exclusion checked individually: docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md, scripts/collect_feedback.py, episodes/, and scripts/verify_worktree_precondition_coverage.py are all unmodified. class TaskFieldCompleteness is byte-identical to HEAD (I extracted both versions and compared, 6635 chars each), _EXCLUDED_FIELDS still contains 'directives' at line 4158, and _flatten is unchanged -- so g2-implement's territory is intact. The single test-file hunk is a pure 154-line insertion of a new class between two existing ones; no existing expected string was reconciled. Engine changes confined to state(), a new sibling formatter pair, and render_human's docstring plus emission site.

r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: Evidence present, fresh, and reproducible -- and I reproduced all of it rather than reading it. RED capture file exists at evidence/g1-RED-capture.txt; my independent revert-and-rerun produced the identical counts (5 failed, 2 passed, 339 deselected, 4 subtests passed, EXIT=1). Post-change 346 passed EXIT=0 reproduced twice. The 17-passed/329-deselected four-class selection reproduced exactly. The before/after current captures exist and I re-derived the same 8-line purely-additive delta two independent ways: against the run's live spine.json through the repo engine, and by loading HEAD's engine as a second module and diffing render output. The implementer's own honesty markers hold up: it flagged the em-dash codepage transcription and pointed at the raw on-disk capture, and it correctly explained why 2 of the 7 tests pass in RED by construction -- which is exactly why I mutation-tested those two separately (see cc3).

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: All three handoff constraints pass (r4a/r4b/r4c above). Inherited crew discipline also holds: minimal change, no speculative abstraction, test-led with a reproduced RED, fail-visibly (an unrecognized shape renders nothing rather than guessing), and the new code matches the surrounding naming and docstring conventions -- the formatter/leaf-speller pair mirrors _render_anchor_lines/_anchor_category_items exactly. One quality observation, non-blocking, recorded at r5: the list branch silently drops non-string items, which is a partial render rather than a visible failure.

r5-reconciliation.title: Reconciliation check
r5-reconciliation.imperative: Does the change diverge from the recorded architecture in a way Commander must reconcile? Record pass/fail; flag a triage candidate if it is out of scope.
r5-reconciliation.finding: No divergence Commander must reconcile. Map Impact notes check out against the diff and the evidence: the structural anchors named are the ones actually touched; the capability claim (current is the complete state channel) is real -- directives was the third and last of the three populated-but-dropped Task fields, anchors and constraints having closed under #420; and assumption:schema-type-is-drifted is confirmed live at docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md:123, which declares [string] | null against 8/8 dict instances in the corpus. That doc is UNMODIFIED, correctly left to g3, and per the handoff I do not block on it -- though note line 138 now carries a second staleness beyond the type row: it asserts 'Known gap, not yet closed: directives, when populated, is not rendered', which this change falsifies. g3 must fix both, not just the type. All three decision anchors are honored, and none of them needed unsettling, so no authority was required. Three triage candidates recorded (tc1-tc3).

r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards — an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json, run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py <record> (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. Before recording pass, fill this item's postcondition command with the real record path you wrote it to -- record() now runs it and refuses `pass` if it fails. Do NOT silently skip this item.

postconditions.statement: verify_fowler_pass.py exits 0 on the Fowler-pass record -- refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override

constraints: Fowler smells are subordinate to documented repo standards; never hard violations
an override (smell not flagged because a standard wins) needs a logged reason
r6-fowler.finding: Full Fowler baseline pass rendered over the working-tree diff; record at .agent-work/b433-render-directives/g1-review/fowler-pass.json. 12 smells visited, none skipped. ONE flagged: speculative-generality -- the dict-value-not-a-dict else branch (1716-1717) handles a shape the implementer states is not in the corpus and no test reaches; I proved it dead against the suite by replacing it with an unconditional raise and still getting 346 passed EXIT=0. Non-blocking observation, not a rework demand. FOUR overridden, each with the winning standard and the reason logged: duplicated-code (decision:own-helper-not-anchors-helper at settled/human, plus the shapes genuinely differ), primitive-obsession (the engine's contract is raw on-disk JSON per docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md), shotgun-surgery (the three edit sites ARE INV-1/INV-2's shape; collapsing them would break the invariant this change is tested against), comments-as-deodorant (the docstrings carry required verification provenance, not explanation of murky code). Seven absent, each with the reason. I also confirmed the rail is not a check that cannot fail: blanking one override.reason on a temp copy produced 'REFUSED: OVERRIDE-LOG ... no override.reason', EXIT=1.

cc1-red-reproduced.title: CC1: golden captured RED before the change (REPRODUCE)
cc1-red-reproduced.imperative: Independently reproduce the RED: revert ONLY scripts/checklist_engine.py, assert it is actually reverted, run the new RenderDirectives tests, confirm they fail, restore the file and assert restoration. Paste real output. Record pass/fail.
cc1-red-reproduced.finding: REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY, not accepted on report. Backed up scripts/checklist_engine.py outside the repo, ran 'git checkout -- scripts/checklist_engine.py', and ASSERTED the mutation applied two ways: 'git diff --quiet' returned clean vs HEAD, and grep counted 0 occurrences of _render_directive_lines (a mutation that silently did not apply would have left a green run reading exactly like a passing guard). Test file left MODIFIED (class RenderDirectives present). RED run: '5 failed, 2 passed, 339 deselected, 4 subtests passed', EXIT=1 -- identical counts to the implementer's claimed capture. The failures are substantive, not import errors: state() raised KeyError 'directives', and the shipped-spine assertIn failure printed the actual pre-change 'current' for the real COMMANDER_SPINE execute gate, showing the replan_input contract genuinely absent from what the agent reads. Restored from backup; md5 a4d1a78d110bd531daf08811f1a69e78 matches pre-revert and 'diff' reports byte-identical.

cc2-first-line-byte-identical.title: CC2: first line of current is byte-identical
cc2-first-line-byte-identical.imperative: Confirm 'ACTIVE {id} [{status}] - {imperative}' is unchanged, and that GoldenOutputBriefing and ShippedTemplates are green AND unmodified by this diff. Record pass/fail.
cc2-first-line-byte-identical.finding: Verified empirically, not by reading the diff. I loaded 'git show HEAD:scripts/checklist_engine.py' as a second module alongside the changed one and rendered current() under both. On the shipped COMMANDER_SPINE execute gate the first line is byte-identical and the unified diff of the FULL output is purely additive: 8 added lines (the directives block, between '0/4 met' and 'next:'), zero removed. Extended tree-wide: 370 checklist files, 2981 gates rendered under both engines -- 8 gates change output (exactly the 8 carrying a populated directives field), and gates whose FIRST LINE changed = 0. GoldenOutputBriefing/ShippedTemplates/TaskFieldCompleteness are each byte-identical to HEAD (extracted both versions and compared strings; 10 passed, 20 subtests passed).

cc3-absent-empty-silent.title: CC3: absent and empty directives add zero output
cc3-absent-empty-silent.imperative: Confirm the test exists AND that it would fail if the guard were removed (mutate the emission guard, watch it go red, restore). Record pass/fail.
cc3-absent-empty-silent.finding: Test exists AND bites. test_absent_or_empty_directives_add_no_output covers five cases (None, {}, [], '' via subTest, plus 'del t[directives]' for a key absent entirely), and test_unrecognized_directives_shape_renders_nothing covers a non-dict non-list scalar. Both PASS pre-change too (they were 2 of the 2 passed in the RED run), so existence alone proves nothing -- I removed the guard to check. Byte-level mutation 'if directive_lines:' -> 'if True:' in render_human (CRLF working tree, so the edit was done on bytes; a naive LF match silently found nothing on the first attempt, exactly the CREW_CONTEXT hazard), asserted present by grep at line 1772. Mutant run: '2 failed, 5 passed, 339 deselected', EXIT=1, and the two failures are precisely these two tests, each diffing a spurious bare 'directives:' header. Restored byte-identical (md5 a4d1a78d...); RenderDirectives back to 7 passed.

cc4-state-pure.title: CC4: state() gained no side effect
cc4-state-pure.imperative: Read the added line in state(); confirm pure passthrough, no check re-runs (INV-2). Record pass/fail.
cc4-state-pure.finding: state() gained exactly one executable line at 1617: '"directives": t.get("directives"),' inside the same dict literal as constraints/anchors. A bare dict .get -- no call, no mutation, no check evaluation. It deliberately does NOT coerce with 'or []' (unlike constraints), matching anchors so None passes through as None and render_human owns all shape handling. The rest of the state() hunk is comment. Behaviourally pinned by test_state_passes_directives_through_without_re_running_checks, which patches E.subprocess.run with side_effect=AssertionError over a gate carrying FAIL_COMMAND -- so any process spawn during state() raises. That test was one of the 5 RED failures I reproduced (KeyError 'directives'), so it is a proven-failing guard, not decoration.

cc5-both-shapes.title: CC5: both corpus shapes render
cc5-both-shapes.imperative: Confirm nested-dict and flat-list-of-strings each have their own test AND that the renderer really serves both. Record pass/fail.
cc5-both-shapes.finding: Both shapes served, each with its own test. Renderer carries an isinstance(directives, dict) branch (1709-1718) and an isinstance(directives, list) branch (1719-1720); tests are test_nested_contract_dict_shape_renders_indented_leaves and test_flat_list_of_strings_shape_renders_one_line_each, and BOTH were among the 5 RED failures I reproduced, so both are proven-failing guards. The flat-list branch is not hypothetical: I confirmed tests/test_checklist_engine.py:4192 sets t['directives'] = ['DIRECTIVE_UNIQUE_TEXT'] in the TaskFieldCompleteness fixture, and 'directives' is still in that class's _EXCLUDED_FIELDS (4158) pending g2 -- so when g2 removes it, a dict-only renderer would fail there. It will not. Also verified the tests share no leaf-extraction helper with the renderer: every expected value is a hard-coded literal string, so a bug in _directive_leaf cannot cancel out against the assertion.

cc6-renderer-wired.title: CC6: the renderer is wired
cc6-renderer-wired.imperative: Confirm _render_directive_lines has at least one real call site outside its own definition, by command not by memory. Record pass/fail.
cc6-renderer-wired.finding: Wired, confirmed by command. grep -n '_render_directive_lines' scripts/checklist_engine.py returns 3 lines: 1616 (a comment in state()), 1689 (the def), 1771 (the real call site inside render_human, immediately after the anchors block). So one genuine call site outside the definition -- matches the implementer's claim. Not shipped-inert: the end-to-end proof is the corpus scan above, where the shipped spine's rendered current() actually gained the replan_input contract; a renderer nothing called could not have changed that output.

cc7-suite-green.title: CC7: full test file green with real exit code
cc7-suite-green.imperative: Run FORCE_COLOR= NO_COLOR=1 python -m pytest -q tests/test_checklist_engine.py; echo EXIT=$?. Capture the REAL exit code. Record pass/fail.
cc7-suite-green.finding: Ran it myself, twice, and read the real exit code from echo EXIT=$? rather than the summary line. Baseline before I mutated anything: '346 passed, 30 subtests passed in 12.16s', EXIT=0. Final run after both mutations were reverted and the file confirmed byte-identical: '346 passed, 30 subtests passed in 15.01s', EXIT=0. Command exactly as specified, FORCE_COLOR= NO_COLOR=1 python -m pytest -q tests/test_checklist_engine.py, using python not py (#454 / CREW_CONTEXT). Matches the implementer's claimed 346.

r4a-docstring-names-shapes.title: Rule: docstring names the corpus shapes verified against
r4a-docstring-names-shapes.imperative: Check _render_directive_lines's docstring names the shapes, as _render_anchor_lines's does.
r4a-docstring-names-shapes.finding: Satisfied, and better than the sibling it copies. The docstring (1690-1708) names both shapes explicitly, cites the inventory it was verified against, names the shipped gate as the concrete instance, states the unrecognized-shape rule in the same words _render_anchor_lines uses, and cites decision:own-helper-not-anchors-helper for why it is not routed through the anchors normalizer. _directive_leaf carries its own docstring justifying bare strings vs JSON spelling. One number is unpinned: the docstring says '2955 gates scanned' with no revision. My own scan at this working tree counted 2981 gates across 370 files -- the difference is files created since (my survey, its manifests, the implement plan), not a wrong claim, but per inherited doctrine a measured number in prose should be pinned to the revision it was measured at. Non-blocking; noted as an observation.

r4b-leaf-extraction-not-shared.title: Rule: test leaf extraction not shared with the renderer's
r4b-leaf-extraction-not-shared.imperative: Check the tests do not call the renderer's leaf speller, so a shared bug cannot cancel out.
r4b-leaf-extraction-not-shared.finding: Satisfied. The tests never call _directive_leaf or _render_directive_lines; every expected value is a hard-coded literal string in an assertEqual over the whole current() output, or an assertIn of a literal block. So the failure mode the constraint guards against -- renderer and assertion sharing a broken extractor and agreeing on nothing -- cannot occur here. Confirmed structurally by the mutation runs: changing the renderer moved the assertions both times.

r4c-no-new-dependency.title: Rule: no new dependency
r4c-no-new-dependency.imperative: Check the diff adds no import.
r4c-no-new-dependency.finding: Satisfied. Grepping the added lines of both files for import statements returns zero. The only module the new code uses is json (json.dumps in _directive_leaf), already imported at line 16 of the pre-change file.

consolidation.summary: APPROVE. All 7 close criteria verified independently; 17/17 survey items pass; no blockers. The load-bearing check holds: I reproduced the RED myself by reverting only scripts/checklist_engine.py, asserting the revert applied two ways, and running the new tests -- 5 failed, 2 passed, 339 deselected, EXIT=1, matching the implementer's claim -- then restored the file byte-identical. I did not accept a single claimed side-effect on report. Two further mutations proved the guards bite: removing the emission guard turns exactly the two silence tests red, and the suite is green (346, EXIT=0) at both baseline and final state. Corpus-wide, the change alters current for exactly the 8 gates carrying a populated directives field and changes zero first lines across 2981 gates. No excluded file touched; TaskFieldCompleteness, GoldenOutputBriefing and ShippedTemplates are byte-identical to HEAD. One non-blocking Fowler finding (an untested defensive branch) and three triage candidates recorded. Working tree left exactly as found; nothing committed.

triage_candidates.statement: The flat-list branch of _render_directive_lines silently drops non-string items: [f'  {item}' for item in directives if isinstance(item, str)]. A mixed list renders partially, so a standing instruction disappears without any signal -- the exact defect class #433 closes, in the fix for it. No corpus instance exists (all 8 populated gates are dicts) and the schema declares [string], so this is latent, not live. But it departs from the docstring's own stated rule (an unrecognized shape renders NOTHING rather than guessing) and from fail-visibly posture. Note _render_anchor_lines's list branch does NOT filter, so the two siblings disagree. Decide whether the shape should render every item via _directive_leaf, or refuse the whole block.

The engine mints a work-area directory keyed on the plan's own work_id, beside the plan rather than under it. Driving this review's survey (work_id b433-render-directives-g1-review, file at .agent-work/b433-render-directives/g1-review/review.json) created .agent-work/b433-render-directives/b433-render-directives-g1-review/ holding context/ and mechanical/ step manifests. The implementer independently hit the same thing from its own plan. Two crew roles tripping the same surprise in one gate makes it a real convention gap: the handoff dictates where the survey file goes, the engine independently derives where its manifests go, and the two do not agree. Engine-written provenance, so neither of us deleted it.

_render_directive_lines's docstring states '2955 gates scanned' with no revision pin. My own scan of the same worktree counted 2981 gates across 370 checklist files -- the delta is files created since the inventory ran, not a wrong claim. Per inherited doctrine (pin a claim to the revision you read it at), a measured number carried in a durable docstring should name the revision it was measured at, or the number will go on being repeated after the tree has moved. The load-bearing half of the claim, 8 populated directives blocks, I reproduced exactly.
